instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company stores about 100 GiB of application data on an Amazon EFS Regional file system that uses Bursting throughput. The file system has used all of its burst credits, and the application slows down. The application drives a steady-state, predictable throughput close to its peak all day. The company has measured this rate over several months and expects it to stay the same. The company must restore the performance of the application. Which change will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep Bursting throughput, and store extra unused data in the file system to raise the baseline throughput that the file system earns.

options.label: B
options.text: Switch the file system to Provisioned throughput, and set the provisioned level to the throughput that the application needs at its peak.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new file system that uses the Max I/O performance mode, and copy the application data to the new file system.

options.label: D
options.text: Switch the file system to Elastic throughput, so that throughput scales up and down with the reads and writes of the application.
